name: Wall push-up
description: Wall push-up for controlled push practice.
instructions: Stand facing a solid wall with hands at chest height.
Bend elbows diagonally back as the chest approaches the wall.
Press away while keeping head, hips and heels aligned.
Move within a comfortable range. Stop the set if technique changes or pain develops.
breathing: Exhale during the effort; inhale on the controlled return. Avoid holding your breath.
mistakes: Rushing the movement or using momentum.
Forcing range or continuing through pain.
safety: Use a clear, non-slip space and secure equipment.
Stop for pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness; seek appropriate guidance.
repsGuidance: Start with 6–10 controlled repetitions, leaving 2–3 comfortable repetitions in reserve; alternate sides evenly.

instructions: Start on hands and knees with wrists below shoulders.
Slowly round the back while breathing out.
Gently lengthen into a small arch while breathing in.
Move within a comfortable range. Stop the set if technique changes or pain develops.
breathing: Breathe slowly throughout; do not force the stretch.
mistakes: Rushing the movement or using momentum.
Forcing range or continuing through pain.
safety: Use a clear, non-slip space and secure equipment.
Stop for pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness; seek appropriate guidance.
repsGuidance: Hold or move for the prescribed time; repeat both sides when applicable.

name: Thoracic rotation
description: Thoracic rotation for controlled mobility practice.
instructions: Lie on the side with knees bent and arms reaching forward.
Open the top arm across the torso as the upper back rotates.
Keep knees together and return without forcing the shoulder.
Move within a comfortable range. Stop the set if technique changes or pain develops.
breathing: Breathe slowly throughout; do not force the stretch.

safety: Use a clear, non-slip space and secure equipment.

repsGuidance: Hold or move for the prescribed time; repeat both sides when applicable.

name: Childs pose
description: Childs pose for controlled mobility practice.
instructions: Kneel on a comfortable surface with knees apart as needed.
Sit hips back only as comfortable and reach arms forward.
Breathe gently without forcing knees or shoulders.
Move within a comfortable range. Stop the set if technique changes or pain develops.

name: Supine hamstring stretch
description: Supine hamstring stretch for controlled mobility practice.
instructions: Lie on the back with one knee bent.
Support the other thigh with hands and gently straighten that knee.
Hold a mild stretch without pulling the toes forcefully.
Move within a comfortable range. Stop the set if technique changes or pain develops.

name: Hip flexor stretch
description: Hip flexor stretch for controlled mobility practice.
instructions: Use a comfortable half-kneeling stance with padding under the rear knee.
Gently tuck the pelvis and shift forward slightly.
Hold without arching the back; repeat both sides.
Move within a comfortable range. Stop the set if technique changes or pain develops.

name: Standing hamstring hinge
description: Standing hamstring hinge for controlled mobility practice.
instructions: Place one heel slightly forward with the knee soft.
Hinge gently at the hips with a long spine.
Hold a mild stretch, then change sides.
Move within a comfortable range. Stop the set if technique changes or pain develops.

name: Ankle rocks
description: Ankle rocks for controlled mobility practice.
instructions: Stand facing a wall in a staggered stance.
Move the front knee forward over the toes while the heel stays down.
Return and repeat both sides without collapsing the arch.
Move within a comfortable range. Stop the set if technique changes or pain develops.

name: Wall calf stretch
description: Wall calf stretch for controlled mobility practice.
instructions: Place hands against a wall and step one foot back.
Keep the rear heel down and toes forward while bending the front knee.
Hold gently, then switch sides.
Move within a comfortable range. Stop the set if technique changes or pain develops.
